dmm-2008-devil-01.title: Complement
dmm-2008-devil-01.body:
The two neighbours of the inspector are a uniformly random pair among the other $11$ people, of whom $3$ are Mafia and $8$ are not. The probability that neither neighbour is Mafia is $\dfrac{\binom82}{\binom{11}2}=\dfrac{28}{55}$, so the probability of at least one Mafia neighbour is $1-\dfrac{28}{55}=\dfrac{27}{55}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{27}{55}$**

dmm-2008-devil-02.title: Count three-digit strings
dmm-2008-devil-02.body:
Write each of $000,\dots,999$ with three digits (leading zeros allowed): each digit has $8$ allowed values, so $8^3=512$ strings avoid $4$ and $7$. Remove $000$ (not positive) to get $511$, and add $1000$ (digits $1,0,0,0$, allowed): $512$.

**Answer: 512**

dmm-2008-devil-03.title: Parity
dmm-2008-devil-03.body:
Color the board like a checkerboard. Every krook move changes the square's color. The corners $(1,1)$ and $(8,8)$ have the same color, so the number of moves must be even. $17$ is odd, so it is impossible: $0$ ways.

**Answer: 0**

dmm-2008-devil-04.title: Divisor count
dmm-2008-devil-04.body:
If $n=q_1^{a_1}\cdots q_r^{a_r}$ then $n$ has $\prod(a_i+1)$ divisors. For this to equal the prime $p$ there can be only one factor: $n=q^{p-1}$ for a prime $q$. The smallest such number uses $q=2$: $n=2^{p-1}$.

**Answer: $2^{p-1}$**

dmm-2008-devil-05.title: Linearity of expectation
dmm-2008-devil-05.body:
The board has area $100$. One dart: 
- inner disk (area $\pi$): probability $\frac{\pi}{100}$, score $10$, contributing $\frac{10\pi}{100}$;
- the annulus $1\le r\le3$ has area $8\pi$, split evenly into the four quadrants (area $2\pi$ each); the quadrant scores $1,2,3,4$ contribute $\frac{2\pi}{100}(1+2+3+4)=\frac{20\pi}{100}$.

Expected score per dart: $\frac{30\pi}{100}=\frac{3\pi}{10}$. By linearity, for three darts: $3\cdot\frac{3\pi}{10}=\frac{9\pi}{10}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{9\pi}{10}$**

dmm-2008-devil-06.title: Count in two stages
dmm-2008-devil-06.body:
Put $X=(0,0)$ and $Y=(8,8)$ on the grid; then $A=(1,3)$, $\nabla=(5,3)$, $B=(6,5)$, $C=(5,7)$. Shortest routes use only moves right and up.

*$X$ to $\nabla$* ($5$ right, $3$ up): $\binom83=56$ routes, minus those through $A$. Through $A$: $X\to A$ has $\binom41=4$ routes and $A\to\nabla$ has $1$ (straight right). So $56-4=52$.

*$\nabla$ to $Y$* ($3$ right, $5$ up): $\binom{8}{3}=56$ routes. Through $B$: $\nabla\to B$ ($1$ right, $2$ up) $3$ routes, $B\to Y$ ($2$ right, $3$ up) $\binom52=10$ routes: $30$. Through $C$: $\nabla\to C$ is $1$ route, $C\to Y$ ($3$ right, $1$ up) is $4$ routes: $4$. No route passes through both. So $56-30-4=22$.

Total: $52\cdot22=1144$.

**Answer: 1144**

dmm-2008-devil-07.title: Eliminate variables
dmm-2008-devil-07.body:
From the second equation $y=1-\frac1z=\frac{z-1}z$, so $\frac1y=\frac z{z-1}$ and the first gives $x=4-\frac z{z-1}=\frac{3z-4}{z-1}$. The third gives $\frac1x=\frac73-z$, so $x=\frac3{7-3z}$. Equate: $\frac{3z-4}{z-1}=\frac3{7-3z}$, i.e. $(3z-4)(7-3z)=3(z-1)$, which simplifies to $9z^2-30z+25=0$, so $z=\frac53$. Then $x=\frac3{7-5}=\frac32$ and $y=\frac{z-1}z=\frac25$. Check: $x+\frac1y=\frac32+\frac52=4$. $xyz=\frac32\cdot\frac25\cdot\frac53=1$.

**Answer: 1**

dmm-2008-devil-08.title: Use the period 140
dmm-2008-devil-08.body:
Number the days $0,1,\dots,364$ (January 1 is day $0$). Alan is off on days $\equiv3\pmod4$, Ben on days $\equiv5,6\pmod7$, Catherine on days $\equiv7,8,9\pmod{10}$. The pattern repeats every $\operatorname{lcm}(4,7,10)=140$ days. Alan's off days are odd, which forces Catherine's residue to be $7$ or $9$; solving the three congruences gives exactly four residues mod $140$: $19,27,47,139$.

The year has $365=2\cdot140+85$ days: in the two full cycles (days $0$–$279$) there are $8$ such days; in days $280$–$364$ (residues $0$–$84$) the residues $19,27,47$ appear: $3$ more. Total $11$.

**Answer: 11**

dmm-2008-devil-10.title: Arithmetic progressions
dmm-2008-devil-10.body:
The conditions say that the four digits $a,b,c,d$ form an arithmetic progression with common difference $\delta$, all in $\{0,\dots,9\}$, with $a\ge1$.
- $\delta=0$: $a=1,\dots,9$: $9$.
- $\delta=1$: $a+3\le9$: $a=1,\dots,6$: $6$. $\delta=2$: $a+6\le9$: $a=1,2,3$: $3$. $\delta=3$: needs $a+9\le9$, $a\ge1$ impossible: $0$.
- $\delta=-1$: $a-3\ge0$: $a=3,\dots,9$: $7$. $\delta=-2$: $a\ge6$: $4$. $\delta=-3$: $a=9$: $1$.

Total $9+6+3+7+4+1=30$.

**Answer: 30**

dmm-2008-devil-11.title: Simplify each term
dmm-2008-devil-11.body:
For any angle $t$: $\cot^3t-\cot t=\cot t(\cot^2t-1)=\dfrac{\cos t}{\sin t}\cdot\dfrac{\cos^2t-\sin^2t}{\sin^2t}=\dfrac{\cos t\cos2t}{\sin^3t}$. Multiplying by $\sin^4t$ gives $\sin t\cos t\cos2t=\tfrac12\sin2t\cos2t=\tfrac14\sin4t$.

With $t=2^k\theta$ the $k$-th term is $\tfrac14\sin(2^{k+2}\theta)$, so the sum is $\tfrac14\sum_{k\ge0}\sin(2^{k+2}\theta)=\tfrac14\sum_{j\ge2}\sin(2^j\theta)=\dfrac a4$.

**Answer: $\dfrac a4$**

dmm-2008-devil-12.title: Generating function trick
dmm-2008-devil-12.body:
If coin $i$ shows heads with probability $p_i$, then $\prod_i(1-p_i+p_ix)$ is the generating function of the number of heads. The probability of an even number of heads is $\dfrac{\prod(1)+\prod(1-2p_i)}{2}=\dfrac{1+\prod_i(1-2p_i)}2$ (evaluate at $x=1$ and $x=-1$).

The coin with $p=\cos\frac{8\pi}{24}=\cos\frac\pi3=\frac12$ has $1-2p=0$, so the product is $0$ and the probability is $\dfrac12$.

**Answer: $\dfrac12$**

dmm-2008-devil-13.title: Inclusion-exclusion
dmm-2008-devil-13.body:
There are $6!=720$ seatings. Let $S_j$ be the sum over choices of $j$ couples of the number of seatings in which those couples sit together (each such couple as a block, $2$ orders): $S_1=3\cdot(5!\cdot2)=720$, $S_2=3\cdot(4!\cdot4)=288$, $S_3=3!\cdot8=48$. The number of seatings with no couple adjacent is $720-720+288-48=240$, so the probability is $\dfrac{240}{720}=\dfrac13$.

**Answer: $\dfrac13$**

dmm-2008-devil-14.title: Divisor counts
dmm-2008-devil-14.body:
A number $2^a3^b5^c\cdots$ has $(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)\cdots$ divisors. Checking all the exponent patterns that give a value below $720$ (with the smaller primes carrying the larger exponents), the largest divisor count is $24$, attained by $360=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5$, $420$, $480$, $504$, $540$, $600$, $630$, $672$. The number $720=2^4\cdot3^2\cdot5$ has $5\cdot3\cdot2=30\ge25$ divisors, so it is the smallest.

**Answer: 720**

dmm-2008-devil-15.title: Write out each set
dmm-2008-devil-15.body:
*$i=1$:* $B_1=\{\varnothing,A_1\}$ has two elements, $C_1=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\},\{A_1\},B_1\}$. $D_1=\{\varnothing,A_1,\{\varnothing\},\{A_1\},B_1\}$; these are pairwise different (they have $0,3,1,1,2$ elements and $\{\varnothing\}\neq\{A_1\}$ since $A_1\ne\varnothing$), so $k_1=5$.

*$i=2$:* $B_2=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}$, $C_2=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\},\{\{\varnothing\}\},B_2\}$, and $D_2=B_2\cup C_2=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\},\{\{\varnothing\}\},B_2\}$: $k_2=4$.

*$i=3$:* $B_3=\{\varnothing,\varnothing\}=\{\varnothing\}$, $C_3=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}$, $D_3=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}$: $k_3=2$.

Product $5\cdot4\cdot2=40$.

**Answer: 40**
